# android_vendor_xiaomi_zephyr

Proprietary blobs for the **Redmi Note 17 4G** — codename `zephyr`, Xiaomi project
`p19a`, SM6225-AF (`bengal`).

Extracted from the stock firmware
`zephyr_global_images_OS3.0.311.0.WBUMIXM_16.0` (HyperOS 3.0.311.0.WBUMIXM,
Android 16 / SDK 36, kernel 5.15.194-android13-8). The blobs were first taken
from 3.0.310.0; 3.0.311.0 changed the content of 84 of them and the inventory
not at all.

**This repo is generated — do not edit it by hand.**

## Contents

```
Android.bp               Soong modules for the ELF blobs
zephyr-vendor.mk         PRODUCT_COPY_FILES / PRODUCT_PACKAGES
BoardConfigVendor.mk     board flags the device tree includes
proprietary/             the blobs themselves
```

3633 blobs, 1.4 GB. 142 Soong modules — 8 of them `install_symlink`, which is how
the Adreno EGL/GLES links, the WCNSS config link, a JNI link and a few
cross-directory links are reproduced — and 3499 product copies, with no
duplicate destinations.

Seven stale face artifacts and the unused `miface.xml` Soong module are also
deliberately absent. The files are `vendor/bin/hw/mifaced`,
`vendor/etc/init/miface.rc`,
`vendor/etc/permissions/android.hardware.biometrics.face.xml`,
`vendor/etc/vintf/manifest/miface.xml`,
`vendor/lib64/android.hardware.biometrics.face-V2-ndk.so`,
`vendor/lib64/libFaceUnlock.so` and `vendor/lib64/libmiface.so`. Nothing in
`zephyr-vendor.mk` installs any of them, and the built vendor image contains no
face HAL, service, permission, VINTF fragment or library. These eight deltas
(seven files plus the unused module) are the only intentional tree difference
from the source vendor directory; every installed blob is identical.

Eight stock files are deliberately absent. `vendor/etc/{passwd,group}` and
`odm/etc/{passwd,group}` are generated by the build from the device tree's
`configs/config.fs` (the stock `group` names AIDs 2901-2914 and the stock `odm`
pair are empty files, so copying them would either collide with or blank the
generated ones). `vendor/etc/NOTICE.xml.gz` and `odm/etc/NOTICE.xml.gz` are
generated per partition from the compliance metadata, and keeping the stock
copies duplicated the path in the image file list.

`vendor/bin/vndservicemanager` and `vendor/etc/init/vndservicemanager.rc` are
absent as well. `frameworks/native` builds that daemon for this release and the
device tree lists it in `PRODUCT_PACKAGES`; the stock prebuilt implements
`IServiceManager` against a different `libbinder` than the one the tree
installs, and aborts in `ServiceManager::listServices`, which leaves
`/dev/vndbinder` without a context manager and no vendor HAL able to register.

Some stock init scripts are rewritten by the device tree's `extract-files.py`
fixups on the way out of the dump: services without a `user` get `user root`
(Android 16's init rejects them outright), and seven services whose HIDL
interface exists only as a blob — `dpmQmiMgr`, `embmssl`, `alarm`, `dsp`,
`factory`, `limits`, `wifilearner` — lose the `interface` line and the
`disabled` flag, so init starts them with their class at boot instead of
lazily.

`vendor/etc/ueventd.rc` is rewritten too. `mi_disp` names its character device
`mi_display/disp_feature` from a class `devnode` callback, and ueventd only keeps
a path of that shape when a `subsystem` block switches `devname` to
`uevent_devpath`. Stock declares that block in its **system** `ueventd.rc`, which
the tree replaces with AOSP's copy, so the fixup adds the `subsystem mi_display`
block and the `/dev/mi_display/* 0666 root graphics` rule here. Without it the
node is created as `/dev/disp_feature`, `0600 root:root`, and the Goodix FOD HAL
cannot open the `/dev/mi_display/disp_feature` path it hardcodes.

Three of the blobs are VINTF fragments for the display stack, and they are here
on purpose: `android.hardware.graphics.mapper-impl-qti-display.xml`,
`vendor.qti.hardware.display.allocator-service.xml` and
`vendor.qti.hardware.display.composer-service.xml`. The device tree dropped them
while the platform still built the sm6225 display HALs (both sides install a
fragment with the same filename, which make rejects as a duplicate target), and
that tree is now pinned out of the manifest because its SDE/DPU code needs the
techpack display headers the kernel drop does not ship. The composer, allocator
and mapper implementations in `vendor/bin/hw/` and `vendor/lib64/` never left, so
with the fragments restored the stock graphics HALs are declared again.

The stock `vendor/bin/toolbox` and `vendor/bin/toybox_vendor` are **not** here.
`base_vendor.mk` pulls in `shell_and_utilities_vendor`, which requires the
platform `toolbox_vendor` and `toybox_vendor`, so `/vendor/bin` already gets
both binaries and the 181 applet symlinks that point at them; shipping the
stock pair as well made the vendor image claim those paths twice, which soong
rejects as a packaging conflict. The device tree's `proprietary-files.txt`
records the omission.

## How it was generated

The blob list, the extraction script and the fixups live in the device tree
[`uzbforce/android_device_xiaomi_zephyr`](https://github.com/uzbforce/android_device_xiaomi_zephyr):

```bash
# device/xiaomi/zephyr
./extract-files.py --keep-dump /path/to/dump   # writes vendor/xiaomi/zephyr
./setup-makefiles.py                           # regenerate the makefiles only
```

The dump is produced by `tools/extract-firmware.sh` in the device tree, which
unsparses `super.img`, unpacks the logical partitions and extracts the EROFS
filesystems.

To refresh after a firmware update: re-extract, run
`tools/check-blob-drift.py` (device tree) to see what the new firmware adds,
drops and changes, run `extract-files.py` from the device tree, restore this
`README.md` — `extract-files.py` wipes everything in here except dot-entries,
which is what prunes dropped blobs but also takes hand-written files with it —
then commit. Keep `proprietary-files.txt` in the device tree: it is the
reviewable artifact, not this repo.

## Device-specific notes

- These blobs are **not** interchangeable with other SM6225 Xiaomi trees. The
  vendor image is a shared `mivendor_sm6225_global` build, but the camera
  modules (`p19A_*`), the THN31 NFC stack, the Goodix FOD firmware, the
  `oca72xxx`/`fs1815` audio configs and the p19a panel XMLs are per-device.
- Camera: OV50D40 / S5KJNSSQ33 (rear), SC1620CS / GC16B3 (front), all four
  module variants are included.
- NFC: THN31 with Xiaomi's TMS HAL (`nfc_nci.thn31nfc.tms.so`), **not** NXP
  SN100/SN220. The SN100/SN220 firmware in `proc` is unused generic payload.

## Usage

Place this repo at `vendor/xiaomi/zephyr` in an Android 16 tree:

```xml
<!-- .repo/local_manifests/vendor.xml; keep it separate from the device tree's
     zephyr.xml, which carries the platform projects -->
<project name="uzbforce/android_vendor_xiaomi_zephyr"
         path="vendor/xiaomi/zephyr"
         remote="github" revision="lineage-23.2" />
```

Then:

```bash
source build/envsetup.sh
lunch lineage_zephyr-bp4a-user
mka bacon
```
